newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan militia says its fighters must grow beards.
newsitem.headline: Afghan militia says its fighters must grow beards.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban opposition has ruled that its fighters must wear beards to conform to strict Islamic principles, a rebel-run newspaper said on Tuesday.
It said the Taleban shura (council) in the newly captured eastern city of Jalalabad had also decided to ban its fighters from smoking and force all women to wear veils outside the home.

"All the victories of the Taleban are owed to the blessings of God and because of that we are bound to follow God and his prophet Mohammad," the newspaper quoted Taleban spokesman Mullah Ahmed Jan, based in the Pakistani city of Peshawar, as saying.

"So all those soldiers in Nangarhar, Laghman and Kunar provinces who do not have beards will be expelled from the army," he said. Taleban fighters too young to grow beards would be sent back to school, he added.

Jan said unspecified action would be taken against Taleban members caught smoking, but the ban did not apply to ordinary people. All women, however, would have to wear what he called Islamic dress and cover their faces outside their homes.
He said the Taleban had imposed a night curfew in Jalalabad.
The Taleban sprang from religious schools in Pakistan and southern Afghanistan two years ago to become the most powerful foes of President Burhanuddin Rabbani's government.
Already in control of more than half of Afghanistan, the Taleban wants to topple Rabbani and replace his moderate administration with their stricter version of Islamic rule.
